non_blocking_notes: The plan's acceptance criterion 8 names the missing-folium skips at tests/test_map_stations.py:179 and :190; the actual pytest run reports them at tests/test_map_stations.py:279 and :290. tests/test_map_stations.py is not in the diff (git diff --name-only 9725f16...d8b4383 lists six paths, none of them that file), so the plan's line numbers were stale rather than the artifact having moved them. Both skips remain skipped and are the only skips.

The three USGS issue-policy tests each re-declare byte-identical first_issue/second_issue Issue objects and the identical rr.pick(...) sparse selection (tests/test_fetch.py, the warn/ignore/raise tests). A module-level constant pair or a small fixture would remove ~45 duplicated lines without weakening any assertion. Stylistic only; the duplication does keep each test readable in isolation.

test_fetch_on_issue_ignore_returns_all_merged_issues_without_warnings and the fetch_by_provider mirror assert `captured_warnings == []` under warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) without an explicit simplefilter("always"). They pass today because pytest installs an always-filter per test, so a regression that re-warned would be caught; but the tests depend on that ambient pytest behaviour rather than stating it. Adding warnings.simplefilter("always") inside the context would make the negative assertion self-standing.

fetch_by_provider computes raw_mode once outside the dict comprehension while fetch computes it inline before the call; both are correct and the asymmetry is minor, but a shared `_raw_mode(raw)` helper (or the same inline placement) would read more uniformly across the two public boundaries.
summary:
PR #140 implements the human decision exactly. src/rivretrieve/_internal/discovery.py adds keyword-only `raw: bool = False` and `on_issue: OnIssue = "warn"` after the existing required keyword-only start/end on both fetch and fetch_by_provider, preserving selection as positional-or-keyword; `raw` is a plain bool at the boundary and is converted with `RawMode.INCLUDE if raw else RawMode.OMIT` before entering _fetch_provider_series, so no bare bool reaches ProviderHandle.observations or driver.drive. OnIssue is imported only under TYPE_CHECKING and, with `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of the module, the runtime annotation stays the string "OnIssue" that the signature test asserts; OnIssue is not exported. src/rivretrieve/__init__.py deletes exactly the one `RawMode` re-export line and nothing else; `git show d8b4383:src/rivretrieve/_internal/observations.py` confirms the enum survives internally with OMIT="omit" and INCLUDE="include", and all seven m9-owned legacy names (ProviderHandle, provider, observations, stations, provider_info, product_info, map_stations) remain in the 17-name public set.

On ADR-0018's invariant: _fetch_provider_series now passes `raw=raw` instead of the hard-coded RawMode.OMIT, and _merge_provider_results is untouched — it still concatenates `result.raw.entries` in result order with no decode, copy, or reconstruction of content/origin, so the boundary bool changes no retained bytes. On the policy-once requirement: the per-series handle.observations calls still hard-code on_issue="ignore", the results are merged, and the single trailing `apply_on_issue(result.issues, on_issue)` replaces the previously hard-coded "warn". There is exactly one apply_on_issue call in the fetch path, so the default is per completed provider result, not per series. Per-series ignoring swallows nothing: _merge_provider_issues is unmodified and appends every non-provenance issue from every result in order (it only dedupes repeated `provenance.*` codes, pre-existing behaviour), and the tests confirm both authored issues survive under every policy.

I verified the claims rather than taking the PR body's word: `uv run pytest -q` gives exactly 1660 passed, 2 skipped (baseline 1654 + six added tests); `uv run ty check src` passes; `uv run ruff format --check` reports 167 files already formatted; `uv run ruff check` passes. Per instructions I did not run uv build. `git log --oneline` shows a single commit `feat: expose fetch retrieval controls` with no attribution or Co-authored-by footer; no tag points at the head; __version__ remains "0.1.49"; pyproject.toml, uv.lock, docs/, CONTEXT.md and .pce/ are absent from the diff; the write-set is exactly the six planned paths; pr-body.md is untracked and the worktree is tracked-clean.

Test quality: the added tests assert behaviour, not execution. The raw tests pin exact byte strings and full SourceCallOrigin equality including url, request_parameters, status_code, retrieved_at and content_type, plus the recorded per-series call order — a mutation that reconstructed origins or reordered entries would fail. The warn test's exact two-element message list is the real proof that policy is applied once after the merge rather than once per series (a per-series application would produce a different count/ordering), and the raise test asserts both series were fetched before the raise, which forbids short-circuiting. The signature test replaces its old absence checks with the full ordered parameter, kind, default and annotation-dict expectations; no pre-existing assertion is weakened or deleted — the two default-path assertions `result.raw == RawPayload(..., entries=())` remain, and the fixture's origin change is the plan-authored one, affecting only test_fetch.py's local recorder. The only pre-existing assertions touched elsewhere are the four RawMode import moves and the package-set edit the plan mandates. Nothing here should stop the merge.
